hunks.baseline: Sudal, a river pirate belonging to the Yangtze River Channel League and Deputy Stronghold Lord of the Water Dragon Stronghold, which held sway over Hubei Province, sat at the bow of a ship cutting swiftly through the current, lost in thought.
hunks.sol: Sudal sat at the bow of the ship as it cut swiftly through the current, lost in thought. He was a river pirate of the Yangtze River Channel League and Deputy Stronghold Lord of the Water Dragon Stronghold, which held sway over Hubei Province.

hunks.baseline: He was the deputy lord of a major stronghold with more than five hundred river pirates under its command. And though it had taken him a long time, he had finally reached the Peak level of martial arts.
hunks.sol: He was deputy lord of a major stronghold with more than five hundred river pirates under its command. And though it had taken him a long time, he had finally reached the Peak level of martial arts.

hunks.baseline: Simply staying active and in one piece as he approached fifty made him a model of a successful river pirate. But Sudal had already achieved more than that.
hunks.sol: Simply staying active and in one piece as he approached fifty made him a model of a successful river pirate. But Sudal had achieved more than that.

hunks.baseline: It was rare for a water stronghold to have hundreds of fighters.
hunks.sol: Few water strongholds had hundreds of fighters.

hunks.baseline: *Could I buy a decent manor somewhere out in Hubei? Though property prices have probably gone up again. Damn it. Do they plate the pillars in gold or something?*
hunks.sol: *Could I buy a decent manor somewhere out in Hubei? Property prices have probably gone up again, though. Fuck. Do they plate the pillars in gold or something?*

hunks.baseline: Sudal stared gloomily at the current, which broke into rough waves around the ship.
hunks.sol: Sudal stared gloomily at the churning water.

hunks.baseline: Sudal had always thought of himself as a born sailor and river pirate.
hunks.sol: Sudal had always prided himself on being a born sailor and river pirate.

hunks.baseline: *We’re fucked.*
hunks.sol: *I’m fucked.*

hunks.baseline: In the end, the inevitable had arrived.
hunks.sol: The inevitable had arrived.

hunks.baseline: “Well, you see, it’s just—”
hunks.sol: “Well, you see, it’s just…”

hunks.baseline: Sudal turned around slowly and looked at the familiar face of his subordinate.
hunks.sol: Sudal turned slowly toward the familiar face of his subordinate.

hunks.baseline: “Are you really that eager to get your ass kicked?”
hunks.sol: “Are you that eager to get your ass kicked?”

hunks.baseline: “Beef, spicy marinade…”
hunks.sol: “Beef. Spicy marinade…”

hunks.baseline: Sudal trailed off and took a deep breath. Recent experience had been teaching him to rediscover the composure he’d forgotten over the past few decades.
hunks.sol: Sudal trailed off and took a deep breath. Recent experience was teaching him to recover the composure he’d forgotten decades ago.

hunks.baseline: “Then one last question. In the middle of the Yangtze, after more than a month without setting foot on land, do you think we can get our hands on marinated beef?”
hunks.sol: “Then one last question. In the middle of the Yangtze, when it’s been well over a month since we set foot on land, can we get our hands on marinated beef?”

hunks.baseline: “They told me to make some if we don’t.”
hunks.sol: “He said to make some if we don’t.”

hunks.baseline: You could always count on him to be the one.
Neither of them said the name, but they both knew who they meant.
hunks.sol: Neither of them said the name, but they both knew.

hunks.baseline: A build and appetite that barely seemed human. A level of simple-mindedness that could shock even the most uncultured river pirates.
hunks.sol: A build and appetite that barely seemed human. Simple-mindedness that could shock even the most uncultured river pirates.

hunks.baseline: Actually, Sudal had once met another lunatic of the same sort, albeit one considerably smaller.
hunks.sol: Actually, Sudal had once met another lunatic of much the same sort, albeit one considerably smaller.

hunks.baseline: The young man who looked perfectly normal, but seemed possessed by some kind of ghost, and would stuff his face with dumplings and sweets whenever he got the chance.
hunks.sol: The young man who looked perfectly normal but seemed possessed by some kind of ghost, stuffing his face with dumplings and sweets whenever he got the chance.

hunks.baseline: Sudal gazed wistfully back on the past, a few months ago, then let out a sigh.
hunks.sol: Sudal gazed wistfully back on those days a few months ago, then let out a sigh.

hunks.baseline: “I’m telling you. The second he made eye contact with you, he’d start whining for candied hawthorn skewers. That son of a bitch was a real pain in the ass.”
hunks.sol: “I’m telling you. The second he made eye contact with you, he’d start whining for those skewers. That *horo* bastard was something else.”[^2]

hunks.baseline: The lunatic who wanted beef was a Peak master from the Black Dragon Demon Gate, one of the foremost factions among the unorthodox. He was also the right-hand man of its Young Sect Leader, who was all but certain to inherit the sect. And that little shit he’d mentioned was a far, far bigger figure than even him.
hunks.sol: The lunatic who wanted beef was a Peak master from the Black Dragon Demon Gate, one of the foremost unorthodox factions. He was also the right-hand man of its Young Sect Leader, who was all but certain to inherit the sect. And the *horo* bastard they’d just mentioned was an even bigger figure.

hunks.baseline: *If it’s Cheongpung, the Huashan Divine Dragon, he’s a big shot among big shots.*
hunks.sol: *Cheongpung, the Huashan Divine Dragon. Now there’s a big shot among big shots.*

hunks.baseline: In terms of seniority alone, he stood on equal footing with the Sect Leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang. And according to public opinion, his talent for martial arts was among the top three throughout history.
hunks.sol: In terms of seniority alone, he stood on equal footing with the Sect Leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang. And according to popular opinion, his talent for martial arts ranked among the top three of all time.

hunks.baseline: “Beef! Taishan wants beef! Spicy sauce!”
hunks.sol: “Beef! Taishan wants beef! Spicy marinade!”

hunks.baseline: Sudal’s subordinate turned pale as he spoke.
hunks.sol: Sudal’s subordinate turned pale.

hunks.baseline: Sudal snapped out of it and told him where he’d hidden his emergency rations for drinking snacks.
hunks.sol: Sudal snapped out of it and told him where he’d hidden his emergency supply of drinking snacks.

hunks.baseline: “There’s a jar in the corner of the cabin I use.”
hunks.sol: “There’s a jar in the corner of my cabin.”

hunks.baseline: “Of course it won’t. With his appetite, he could eat the whole jar and still want more. But what if you take it over with the Young Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate?”
hunks.sol: “Of course not. With his appetite, I wouldn’t be surprised if he ate the jar too. But what if you went with the Young Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate?”

hunks.baseline: “That’s our Deputy Stronghold Lord, all right!”
hunks.sol: “That’s our Deputy Stronghold Lord!”

hunks.baseline: The subordinate raised a thumb and hurried off. Sudal watched him go with a proud smile and rubbed the bridge of his nose.
hunks.sol: The subordinate gave him a thumbs-up and hurried off. Sudal watched him go with a proud smile and rubbed the bridge of his nose.

hunks.baseline: But the smile disappeared in an instant.
hunks.sol: But the smile vanished.

hunks.baseline: He’d even felt proud of himself for coming up with a decent solution. Now, all of a sudden, the misery welled up in him, and his eyes grew wet.
hunks.sol: He’d even felt proud of himself for coming up with a decent solution. The misery suddenly welled up in him, and his eyes grew wet.

hunks.baseline: A sudden sense of futility weighed on him, but Sudal forced himself to shake his head.
hunks.sol: For a moment, doubt gripped him. Sudal forced himself to shake his head.

hunks.baseline: It had already been five days since they left Yunnan. With the heavens on their side, and a good wind, they could arrive within a day.
hunks.sol: It had already been five days since they left Yunnan. With heaven’s help and a good wind, they might arrive within a day.

hunks.baseline: Sudal snapped out of his thoughts and blinked. An old man who looked stern as hell stood before him, holding a fishing rod.
hunks.sol: Sudal blinked, shaken from his thoughts. An old man who looked stern as hell stood before him, holding a fishing rod.

hunks.baseline: “You’re…”
hunks.sol: “You…”

hunks.baseline: “Me?”
hunks.sol: “You?”

hunks.baseline: “……What should I call you, then?”
hunks.sol: “…What should I call you, then?”

hunks.baseline: “Just call me Senior No. And get that hideous face of yours away from the bow. The Dragon King would turn tail if he came up here for some fresh air and saw your mug.”
hunks.sol: “Just call me Senior No. And get that hideous face of yours away from the bow. The Dragon King would turn tail if he came up for some fresh air and saw your mug.”

hunks.baseline: Now, five days into their voyage back, Sudal still didn’t know exactly who he was. But looking at him now, the old man somehow gave off the air of a master.
hunks.sol: Now, five days into their voyage back, Sudal still didn’t know exactly who he was. But looking at him, the old man somehow gave off the air of a master.

hunks.baseline: The old man’s forehead was black as if it had been painted, and swollen to twice the size of anyone else’s. Sudal couldn’t take his eyes off it.
hunks.sol: The old man’s forehead was black as if it had been painted, and swollen to twice its normal size. Sudal couldn’t take his eyes off it.

hunks.baseline: If he could get on the good side of the mysterious old master who’d been living in seclusion in Nanman and obtain the formula for a martial art, what better fortuitous encounter could there be?
hunks.sol: If he could get on the good side of a mysterious old master who’d been living in seclusion in Nanman and obtain the formula for a martial art, what better fortuitous encounter could there be?

hunks.baseline: Silence settled at once after that single sentence.
hunks.sol: Silence fell at once.

hunks.baseline: Sudal stared at the old man before him, who already looked like he was out of his mind.
hunks.sol: Sudal stared at the old man, who already looked like he was out of his mind.

hunks.baseline: “Great Hero? What nonsense. That Ironblood Elder is the lowest of the low. One of the scum of the Murim who absolutely must be hunted down and killed. Though he might already be dead. He spent the entire Great Faction War pretending to sit on the sidelines, while he was up to all kinds of dirty business behind the scenes.”
hunks.sol: “Great Hero? What nonsense. That Ironblood Elder is the lowest of the low. Scum who ought to be hunted down and killed for the good of Murim. Though he might already be dead. He spent the entire Great Faction War pretending to sit on the sidelines, while he was up to all kinds of dirty business behind the scenes.”

hunks.baseline: The old man puffed out his chest and replied.
hunks.sol: The old man puffed out his chest.

hunks.baseline: “That’s right. This Namho is none other than the very man standing before you.”
hunks.sol: “That’s right. I’m *the* Namho.”

hunks.baseline: The old man, Namho, smiled fondly as he thought back on his youth. Sudal wondered.
hunks.sol: Namho smiled fondly as he thought back on his youth. Sudal wondered.

hunks.baseline: Perhaps because he was an old master from the previous generation, but Sudal couldn’t recall ever hearing that name.
hunks.sol: Perhaps he was an old master from the previous generation. Sudal couldn’t recall ever hearing the name.

hunks.baseline: Then the old man spoke again, and Sudal, who’d been unsure, couldn’t help but jump in shock.
hunks.sol: But what Namho said next made him jump.

hunks.baseline: “Wow! A thousand, and two thousand more! A hero born of the Great Faction War!”
hunks.sol: “Wow! A thousand, then another two thousand! A hero born of the Great Faction War!”

hunks.baseline: “Sure, the Nine Sects and One Gang? The Five Great Families? They’re strong, very strong. But charging in and swinging a blade isn’t the only thing that matters. What matters is victory in battle!”
hunks.sol: “The Nine Sects and One Gang? The Five Great Families? They’re strong, very strong. But charging in and swinging a blade isn’t the only thing that matters. What matters is victory in battle!”

hunks.baseline: “When I was young, whenever I sent out a messenger pigeon, the great sects everyone had heard of would move, huh? And sometimes the Three Saints and Ten Kings would rush right out!”
hunks.sol: “When I was young, all I had to do was send out a messenger pigeon and the great sects everyone’s heard of would move. Sometimes even the Three Saints and Ten Kings would come rushing out!”

hunks.baseline: Sudal stared at Namho, who remained completely unashamed. After a brief silence, he parted his lips.
hunks.sol: Sudal stared at Namho, who looked entirely pleased with himself. After a brief silence, he spoke.

hunks.baseline: “Martial artists have it filthy dangerous and hard. When they’re young, they show off and get stabbed to death. When they’re old, they’re practically guaranteed to end up with their bodies wrecked.”
hunks.sol: “Being a martial artist is dangerous as hell, and hard work. When you’re young, you show off and get stabbed to death. When you’re old, your body’s a wreck.”

hunks.baseline: “Look at you. You’re trembling right now. You’re getting old, your martial arts are mediocre, and your body’s starting to give out. Might be a stroke, so if you’re interested, come along. I’m on my way to see a famous physician.”
hunks.sol: “Look at you. You’re trembling right now. You’re getting old, your martial arts are mediocre, and your body’s starting to give out. Might be a stroke, so if you’re interested, come along. I’m on my way to see a good physician.”

hunks.baseline: Sudal had already lost it. But he wasn’t trembling from a stroke—he was trembling with rage.
hunks.sol: Sudal’s body had already given out on him. But he wasn’t trembling from a stroke—he was trembling with rage.

hunks.baseline: The last thread of reason he had left was moving his lips to resolve one final question.
hunks.sol: He held on to his last thread of reason long enough to ask one final question.

hunks.baseline: “But if you haven’t even learned Iron Head Technique, why is your forehead so—”
hunks.sol: “But if you haven’t learned Iron Head Technique, why is your forehead so—”

hunks.baseline: “Some beastly bastard disturbed a Black Gold Bee’s hive because he wanted the honey, and I nearly died for it. We somehow managed to draw out the venom, but this swelling just won’t go down.”
hunks.sol: “Some beastly bastard disturbed a Black Gold Bee hive because he wanted the honey, and I nearly died for it. We somehow managed to draw out the venom, but this swelling just won’t go down.”

hunks.baseline: As Namho gently rubbed his black, swollen forehead, Sudal felt the world go dizzy, as though he’d been stung by a bee himself.
hunks.sol: Namho gently rubbed his black, swollen forehead. Sudal felt dizzy, as though he’d been stung by a bee himself.

hunks.baseline: A whole two months. He’d left the merchant ships laden with wealth and grain behind, and under what was practically a threat, he’d been dragged away from his home base in Hubei to Sichuan, and then all the way to Yunnan.
hunks.sol: A whole two months. He’d left merchant ships laden with wealth and grain behind and, under what was practically a threat, been dragged from his home base in Hubei to Sichuan, then all the way to Yunnan.

hunks.baseline: The waiting had gone on forever. He’d stopped in Guangxi for a chance to make some pocket money, only to be caught by the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang—who was known as the Blood Monk—and dragged along.
hunks.sol: The waiting had dragged on forever. He’d stopped in Guangxi for a chance to make some pocket money, only to be caught and dragged along by Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King—who was going by the name Blood Monk.

hunks.baseline: It was easy to call it two months, but being trapped on a ship with the ugliest, most uneducated people in the world had made those two months feel like two years.
hunks.sol: It was easy to call it two months, but being trapped on a ship with the ugliest, most uncultured people in the world had made those two months feel like two years.

hunks.baseline: *All I have to do is take them to Sichuan, then I can go back to Hubei. And this is what happens at the very end.*
hunks.sol: *All I have to do is take them to Sichuan, then I can go back to Hubei. And this is how things are going right to the end.*

hunks.baseline: One beast of a man spent all day shoving whatever he could into his mouth. This time, he’d been tricked by a powerless old man he’d never met before and showered with insults.
hunks.sol: One beast of a man spent all day shoving whatever he could into his mouth. Now Sudal had been fooled by a powerless old man he’d never met before and insulted for his trouble.

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin—the one he’d already seen enough times to know—was going around preaching some religion called the Earth Mother Goddess, or something. Song Ilseom and Sama Pyo, who’d looked like they disliked each other from the start, had dueled on deck and half destroyed the mast.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin—whom he’d met enough times to recognize—was going around preaching some religion called the Earth Mother Goddess to his subordinates. Song Ilseom and Sama Pyo, who’d looked like they disliked each other from the start, had dueled on deck and half destroyed the mast.

hunks.baseline: And Ju Hwaran, the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes and the most beautiful woman in Sichuan?
hunks.sol: And Ju Hwaran, one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes and the most beautiful woman in Sichuan?

hunks.baseline: Just two months ago, when they’d set out for Nanman, she’d looked like a fairy. Now she spent her days coming out onto the deck to keep an eye on everyone.
hunks.sol: Two months ago, when they’d set out for Nanman, she’d looked like a fairy. Now she spent her days coming out onto the deck to watch everyone.

hunks.baseline: And whenever she heard even the slightest sound somewhere, she’d prick up her ears and mutter as though she wanted everyone to hear.
hunks.sol: Whenever she heard even the slightest sound, she’d prick up her ears and mutter loudly enough for everyone to hear.

hunks.baseline: *Oh. That rope scraping is so loud. Should I just cut every rope so the Pavilion Master can be comfortable?*
hunks.sol: *Oh. That rope scraping is so loud. Should I just cut all the ropes so the Pavilion Master can rest?*

hunks.baseline: He’d been patient long enough. Five days of seeing things he couldn’t stand and hearing things he didn’t want to hear.
hunks.sol: He’d put up with enough. For five days, he’d seen everything he never wanted to see and heard everything he never wanted to hear.

hunks.baseline: Overcome with fury, Sudal drew the broad-bladed saber tucked into his waistband.
hunks.sol: Overcome with fury, Sudal reached for the broad-bladed saber tucked into his waistband.

hunks.baseline: Or, he tried to.
Until a familiar voice sounded behind him.
hunks.sol: He was about to draw it when a familiar voice sounded behind him.

hunks.baseline: “Whew. I feel so much better after getting a good rest. Hey, mister, how far have we come?”
hunks.sol: “Whew. I feel a lot better after that rest. Hey, mister, how far have we come?”

hunks.baseline: Sudal slowly turned around. He looked up at Jin Taekyung, who’d shown himself for the first time in five whole days, and answered with a grin.
hunks.sol: Sudal turned slowly. Jin Taekyung had shown himself for the first time in five whole days. Sudal raised his eyes to him and answered with a grin.

hunks.baseline: [^1]: Candied hawthorn skewers are a traditional Chinese street snack made by coating hawthorn fruit with hardened sugar.
hunks.sol:
[^1]: Candied hawthorn skewers are a traditional Chinese street snack made by coating hawthorn fruit with hardened sugar.
[^2]: The Korean name for the snack, *bingdanghoro*, lets the speaker repeat *horo*, an insult meaning “bastard.”
